record.title: A systematic review maps specification, verification, and enforcement gaps in LLM agent safety
record.summary: A June 2026 preprint surveys safety methods for LLM agents that take multi-step actions. The authors report a PRISMA 2020 review of 38 studies and organize the field around specification, verification, and enforcement. Their synthesis identifies errors in translating natural-language requirements into formal rules as a major bottleneck and notes that action-level blocking does not necessarily yield safe task completion. The strongest verifier-tax result comes from one study of tau-bench Airline/Retail tasks: in that study, per-proposal interception reached 94.1% in one setting while safe-success rates were below 5% in most tested configurations; the authors also report 2.0–2.8× token inflation for their Triad architectures. The study used two open-weight models, different 15/30-turn caps, and an unseeded stochastic user simulator, and has no independent reproduction identified. The survey itself was unregistered and conducted by a single reviewer without an inter-rater check, so it is useful field orientation rather than a settled comparative assessment.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report a PRISMA 2020 rapid review of 38 English-language studies published from 2022 to 2026, searched across six databases with eight primary search strings and supplementary searches covering 22 named systems. They introduce a taxonomy spanning specification, verification, and enforcement.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Within that review, the authors characterize natural-language-to-formal specification as a major bottleneck and report semantic correctness of 24% to 35% in the included translation work. They describe runtime monitoring as the most mature enforcement cluster, while emphasizing that it does not provide complete task-level safety guarantees.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The cited verifier-tax preprint reports, on tau-bench Airline/Retail tasks with GPT-OSS-20B and GLM-4-9B, that per-proposal interception reached 94.1% in one GPT-OSS-20B Retail setting while safe-success rates were below 5% in most model/architecture/domain settings (one GLM-4-9B Airline/Triad cell was 5.3%). It reports 2.0–2.8× agent-token inflation for its Triad architectures. These are author-reported, benchmark-specific results from 2,970 trajectories under model-dependent 15/30-turn caps and an unseeded stochastic Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct user simulator; there is no independent reproduction identified.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors disclose that the review was not preregistered and was conducted by one reviewer without an inter-rater reliability check; they identify selection and extraction bias as threats to validity.

evidence_gaps.description: The review's inclusion and extraction decisions have no second-reviewer reliability check; the protocol was not preregistered, and the authors acknowledge possible selection and extraction bias.

The verifier-tax result is drawn from one study, rated Low certainty by the survey authors, and has no independent replication identified. Its underlying experiment used two models, Airline/Retail tau-bench tasks, unequal 15/30-turn caps, an unseeded stochastic user simulator, and no code/data repository linked from the arXiv record.
The review was submitted on June 22, 2026; it does not account for work that appeared after its search cutoff or establish that its taxonomy remains exhaustive.

brief.importance_rationale: If the review's synthesis is representative, it can redirect agent-safety evaluation toward semantic specification quality and task-level safe completion rather than action blocking alone. Its moderate scope, heterogeneous primary studies, single-reviewer method, and low-certainty verifier-tax result make it useful field orientation rather than a paradigm-level result.
limitations: This is an author-reported literature synthesis, not an independent evaluation of safety systems; its quantitative summaries inherit the settings and methods of the included papers.

The verifier-tax result comes from one study, has Low GRADE certainty in the review, and has no independent replication identified. Its 94.1% interception result is per proposed action in one setting, not a rate of tasks made safe; do not generalize it or the below-5% safe-success figures beyond the tested tau-bench tasks and models.
The review uses a single reviewer, has no inter-rater reliability measure, was not preregistered, and includes English-language full-text studies only.
The paper's June 2026 search window means it cannot establish the state of work published later.

The underlying verifier-tax experiment uses model-dependent 15/30-turn caps and an unseeded stochastic user simulator; the arXiv record links no code or data repository. Its token overhead is specific to the reported Triad architecture and tokenizer accounting.
brief.summary: A June 2026 preprint surveys safety methods for LLM agents that take multi-step actions. The authors report a PRISMA 2020 review of 38 studies and organize the field around specification, verification, and enforcement. Their synthesis identifies errors in translating natural-language requirements into formal rules as a major bottleneck and notes that action-level blocking does not necessarily yield safe task completion. The strongest verifier-tax result comes from one study of tau-bench Airline/Retail tasks: in that study, per-proposal interception reached 94.1% in one setting while safe-success rates were below 5% in most tested configurations; the authors also report 2.0–2.8× token inflation for their Triad architectures. technical.claimed_result: The authors synthesize 38 studies into a specification-verification-enforcement taxonomy and identify natural-language-to-formal specification and task-level enforcement as unresolved bottlenecks.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint documents the authors' review protocol, taxonomy, synthesis, and disclosed limitations. It does not independently validate the included studies or establish a general safety guarantee for deployed agents.
technical.mechanism: The review separates specification acquisition, verification, and enforcement, then compares studies by verification stage, representation, task domain, reported evidence, and enforcement outcome. It argues that semantic specification errors can undermine later verification, and that blocking unsafe actions may lead agents to alternative unsafe paths without a task-level success measure.
technical.regime: Rapid English-language review of 38 studies on multi-step LLM-agent plan specification, verification, enforcement, and safety monitoring, published 2022-2026; six named scholarly databases plus supplementary searches.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares a fragmented literature with its own three-stage taxonomy; it does not present a matched experimental baseline or a new agent-system benchmark.

brief.title: A systematic review maps specification, verification, and enforcement gaps in LLM agent safety
brief.why_it_matters: The review puts specification quality and task-level outcomes alongside verifier strength when assessing agent safety. This helps prevent action-block rates from being treated as a substitute for safe task completion, while its own evidence and review-method limits remain material.
